name: slide-title
text: One relation can live inside many objects.
textPreview: One relation can live inside many objects.

text:
2 minutes 15 seconds. The query expression is language-neutral: edge(A, y) asks for the values related to A. Hold the logical relation fixed. Ask students to name the verb each object actually offers. A hash map relies on key hashing and equality before returning the stored value; a B-tree relies on an ordering relation and supports ordered/range access; an adjacency-list graph exposes neighbor traversal. These are not three query languages and they are not three answers. They are three physical realizations whose primitive work differs. The figures are illustrative, not a claim that every implementation uses exactly these layouts. Transition: what lets us say that all three still represent the same edge relation?

name: slide-title
text: A model says what every object means.
textPreview: A model says what every object means.

text:
2 minutes. The model is the contract between representation and logic. In this set-semantics example, both physical objects denote the same two facts: edge(A,B) and edge(A,C). The query is interpreted over those facts and therefore returns B and C. The semantic model is not another storage layout and it is not a performance promise; it tells us what answers are correct. Later the course will define database instances, valuations, CQs, and Datalog more carefully. For now, ask whether changing bucket positions or graph node IDs changes the database meaning. It does not if the representation mapping yields the same logical facts. Transition: a system still needs executable code that preserves this contract.

name: slide-title
text: A compiler turns meaning into object operations.
textPreview: A compiler turns meaning into object operations.

text: typed transformations preserve meaning while changing the program
textPreview: typed transformations preserve meaning while changing the program

text:
2 minutes 30 seconds. Programming languages give us a disciplined way to bridge meaning and machine operations: define semantics, represent programs as typed intermediate values, and lower those values into executable code. The three right-hand fragments are representation-specific examples. HashMap::get uses the hash-map contract; BTreeMap::range uses key ordering; Graph::neighbors uses adjacency. The slide does not claim a compiler chooses among these exact Rust types at runtime. It assumes a representation has been supplied or selected and shows the code that can be generated for it. An interpreter could execute the typed model through generic dispatch; this course emphasizes compilation because the chosen operations become inspectable and optimizable program structure. Transition: semantic preservation gives correctness, but not a good program.

name: slide-title
text: A correct program can still waste work.
textPreview: A correct program can still waste work.

text:
2 minutes 15 seconds. All six paths on this slide can be semantically correct. The left side nevertheless duplicates a compatible source-key index for Q1 and Q2 and builds another structure for a one-shot small query. The right side shares one compatible index across Q1 and Q2 and lets Q3 scan without paying a new build cost. Whether sharing or skipping is legal depends on schema, key, semantics, updates, lifetime, and memory; the figure is a workload-level motivation, not a universal rule. The course project explicitly derives index requirements and tests compatible sharing. Ask students which resource is wasted on the left: both storage and build time. Transition: even after removing avoidable duplication, the best representation still depends on the data itself.

name: slide-title
text: Data shape changes the sensible program.
textPreview: Data shape changes the sensible program.

text:
2 minutes 15 seconds. The logical query is the same on both sides: return each middle node y with edge(A,y) and edge(y,B). Under set semantics this is OUT[A] intersect IN[B]. For sparse adjacency, iterating a short neighbor list and testing membership can avoid touching absent edges. For denser data, fixed-width or compressed bitsets can turn the same intersection into word-, SIMD-, or GPU-parallel operations. The eight-bit vectors are a visible toy; they do not claim one universal machine instruction or a universal crossover point. Density, cardinality, skew, representation cost, memory, and hardware determine the winner. This is why query optimization needs facts about the data shape, not only the query text.

text:
2.5 minutes. Read the bridge left to right. Mini-LINQ is the query surface used in this course; its early typed meaning is based on conjunctive-query and Datalog ideas. The compiler then moves through several typed IRs. Each IR makes a different contract explicit while preserving meaning; physical choice adds shape, bounds, indexes, and algorithms. The emitted Rust program is where work becomes measurable through counters and hardware behavior. The course therefore studies the entire bridge, not only a query notation or only a runtime loop.

3 minutes. Ask for a prediction before reading the two numbers: should forcing compilation help this short aggregate? The PostgreSQL documentation reports 0.365 ms without JIT and 7.416 ms after lowering the JIT threshold for this same example. The reported JIT work totals 7.104 ms, so compilation dominates. These are documentation-example timings from one run, not a universal benchmark and not evidence that JIT is generally harmful. The lesson is conditional: compilation has an upfront cost and is valuable when enough repeated execution can repay it.
